name: MCG -02-22-22, SN 2001ir field (Hubble)
blurb: MCG -02-22-22, a spiral galaxy that hosted the supernova SN 2001ir, seen by Hubble.
label: sn2001irhost-hubble
story: SN 2001ir was a Type IIn supernova, its light marked by narrow hydrogen lines. Years later Hubble returned to the spot to see whether the star that exploded had truly vanished.

claims.text: MCG -02-22-22 is an Scd-type (spiral) galaxy; SN 2001ir lies at 8h36m28.12s -11 50 03.5 (matches the pointing)
SN 2001ir is of type IIn, with a spectrum dominated by narrow hydrogen lines
Hubble program 17731 images old Type IIn sites years later to see whether the progenitor disappeared; SN2001IR is a target
